description: rnews_main.rs:211-213: let now_ms = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_millis() as u64; The .unwrap_or_default() silently uses 0ms if the system clock is before Unix epoch. For the HLC seed this means the clock starts at epoch 0 and the first real SystemTime::now() call in the article loop will be a large forward jump — HLC handles this gracefully by advancing to wall_ms. Less dangerous than the GC ingested_at_ms case (stoa-xrd4u.7) but still undocumented. Add a comment: // Safety: duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) fails only if system clock is before 1970; // HlcClock::new handles a seed of 0 by advancing to wall_ms on first send(). Or use .expect() with a message that identifies the site.
title: rnews_main: unwrap_or_default on HLC seed SystemTime needs a comment
